correctness.rationale: For a planar convex support function in \(W^{1,2}\), the weak area formula gives the positive summable Fourier defect weights. Uniform random reflections project each higher harmonic onto an axis-determined one-dimensional subspace. Independent angular increments have squared moments \(1/2\) and \(3/8\); distinct harmonic squared factors have crossed moment \(1/4\), giving exact finite- and infinite-spectrum covariance by Tonelli. Conditional mean contraction gives the temporal factor. The sharp upper variance equality is exactly the one-frequency condition. The normalized process is a nonnegative martingale; the logarithmic mode multiplier has mean \(-\log 2\), and a Fatou tail bound forces its almost-sure limit to zero for arbitrary summable spectra. The actual standalone verifier independently checked one- and two-step moments, direct area integral, and equality. This supports the all-body proof; finite checks alone would not prove it.

value.rationale: This complete planar convex-body theorem supplies two-time stochastic area covariance rather than an expected contraction alone, with sharp equality classification by a single harmonic. It reveals nonuniform integrability: typical mean-normalized deficits vanish almost surely despite preserved expectation, while coefficient of variation explodes exponentially. These describe structurally different aspects of convergence to the disk and give exact benchmarks for geometric symmetrization algorithms without arbitrary parameter slicing or dependence on finite numerical enumeration.
